title: Justice's Assault
text: “So, getting back to it, what about the remaining forty percent of the men? Do they actually want to be tortured?”
“That’s excluding those, so thirty percent is because they’re tough enough to be useful as manpower.”
“And the last ten percent?”

“No comment. Well, if Shion’s fine with it, I could arrange something. The amount of money offered was pretty impressive. Though when it comes to that sort of thing, Theo in his demi-human form tends to fetch a higher rate.”
“Hey.”

Crocodile Guy furrowed his brow, looking genuinely troubled by something. And so, amid such idle chatter, tonight’s slave trading proceeded apace. Or so I thought—but partway through hopping between mansions and secret auction venues around town, one of the monster dealer’s subordinates came rushing over to us.
“What’s wrong?”
“W-well, actually…”
The monster dealer’s subordinate whispered something into Father’s ear. Father let out a deep sigh.
“We still had more business to discuss, but I think we’d better head back… Please pass along my apologies to the other party.”
“Yes, sir!”
The subordinate saluted and hurried off toward wherever he’d been heading before.
“What is the matter, I wonder?”
“Trouble back at the tent, it seems. Might be more ironic to call it an assault by the Allies of Justice, wouldn’t it?”
“Is everything alright?”
“For now, I suppose. Anyway, we need to hurry back.”
“Not really following, but let’s go back.”
I agreed with Yuki-chan’s words entirely. And so we changed our plans and headed back to the tent.
“Itsuki.”

The moment we returned to the circus tent, Father called out to Itsuki and Rabbit Guy, who seemed to have been waiting right in the center of the tent for just this moment. Oh? Panda’s family was also standing nearby, waiting with what sounded like sighs. Whatever could have happened? As I wondered this, I noticed a pile of Smoked Meats lying paralyzed on the ground.
“Ah, Naofumi-san. Did you come all the way back for this? It’s nothing out of the ordinary, really, hardly worth an urgent report, don’t you think?”
“I don’t think we can just let it slide.”
“What in the world happened here?”
I could tell that somehow the Smoked Meats had run into Itsuki and ended up sprawled on the ground like this, but the actual sequence of events was a complete mystery to me.

“What happened, you ask? Well, not long after you all left, these guys suddenly burst in shouting, ‘We are the Bow Hero’s companions! We have discovered a terrible criminal here! We have come to bring down the hammer of justice in the name of righteousness!’”
Rabbit Guy explained the situation.
“Right, I heard that much too, but then what, Itsuki…”
Since these were Itsuki’s former subordinates, I felt like I could pretty much guess what happened next just from looking at the scene, but Father seemed to be asking just to make sure.

“At first, Naofumi-san, it was your aides who responded, but naturally their target was obviously me from the start. When I had a hunch and casually poked my head out to check, they acted like they’d struck gold and tried to kill me without so much as a word of explanation.”
“They broke past our attempts to restrain them and quite literally lunged at him.”
Apparently the Siltvelt envoy had been injured and was currently receiving treatment for the wound.
“Bhuu.”
Lazy Pig, meanwhile, was completely unscathed—must have slipped away to safety in the nick of time. This is exactly the sort of moment where it’s supposed to step up front to buy everyone else time.
“Some weirdo came at me screaming something strange too… ‘This time I won’t lose to you!’ or whatever.”
Seemed Panda had also been targeted for some reason.
“Didn’t you make some enemies somewhere, Larsa…?”
Elephant asked Panda.
“Well, that’s just how it goes when you’re a mercenary… no wait, I don’t know these guys at all. Can’t recall ever meeting them.”
“‘This time,’ they said—sounds like there’s some grudge from somewhere weird.”
“Hah! When you’re a mercenary, you’re bound to pick up a grudge or two somewhere along the way! Can’t go worrying about every little thing. What, you gonna scold me over something this small?”
Panda furrowed her brow and directed this at her adoptive father and grandfather.
“I’m not saying that much. Even I’ve had a grudge or two held against me.”
“No point worrying about being resented by the likes of those guys. If they come at you, just scatter them, that’s all.”
Neither her adoptive father nor her grandfather seemed inclined to scold Panda at all. But Panda, apparently expecting to be reprimanded, had gone and made a snide remark anyway.
“Seems like I’ve started giving pretty cynical answers lately. You two think I’m being forced into this against my will or something?”
“You’ve been given a fair share of work, that much is true. If you don’t like it, you could always quit.”
“I—I’m not saying anything like that! I’ll see through whatever job I’m given, no question.”
“Oh my.”
“Elmelo, don’t you start talking like that old drunkard too!”
Panda didn’t seem to have any actual complaints about the work itself. Elephant, meanwhile, was covering her mouth and laughing, clearly teasing Panda over her reaction.
“What’s so funny! Quit making fun of me already! Shouldn’t we hurry up and hear the rest of the story?”
“Right. So, these guys… definitely Itsuki’s old companions, I take it, but what exactly were they after by coming here?”

“They had such a desperate look on their faces, saying, ‘For the crime of impersonating Itsuki-sama’s name, and for piling further wickedness atop that, we shall bring down the hammer of justice upon you!’”
Itsuki gave the Smoked Meat a hard kick to the face. Since he wasn’t using his bow, it barely did any damage, but he wore a bold, unshakeable grin all the same.
“—Guh, you… you damn… impostor, you—! I’ll, k-kill—”

That last part was clearly meant to be “kill.” Still paralyzed and unable to move, he nonetheless seemed absolutely determined to convey his murderous intent toward Itsuki, struggling desperately to rise all the while.
“B-Boo, boo… boo-hee.”
“Oh, now we’re begging for our life, are we—‘I always believed in you, Itsuki-sama, I’m sorry I couldn’t speak honestly, it was all because Mald and the others threatened me’—something like that…”
“I see, I see. And then? What exactly were the great and glorious companions of the Bow Hero’s party planning to do?”
Itsuki wore a smile that didn’t reach his eyes in the slightest, the picture of someone politely listening along.
“Boo, boo… boo-boo-boo, boo.”

The pig who’d once been one of Itsuki’s companions squealed out something. Father knit his brow, narrowed his eyes, and gave it a look of pity. Meanwhile, Itsuki kept signaling repeatedly for someone to come knock these guys out from behind. Well, can’t be helped. Might as well follow Itsuki’s instructions. Sleep Lance should do the trick, I gestured from behind, and when he nodded in approval, I got to it.
“Take this, I say!”
“B-Boo-hyah!?”
“Ha, serves you right! Itsuki-sama, please believe—”
“Like I’d ever believe you! Motoyasu-san, oh, and it’s fine to call this one Mald, right? Please don’t let just that one fall asleep. I want to hit him with a fresh wave of despair.”
Itsuki gave a little thumbs-up gesture across his throat, so I promptly knocked him out cold.
“Whew… getting my revenge in like this really isn’t half bad. Ha ha ha. I wanted to see that face of despair as he passed out, thinking he’d been betrayed!”

For some reason, in this moment Itsuki reminded me strongly of how Father had been back in our original world. There seemed to be no room left for us to interject in this exchange between Itsuki and his former companions.
“Now then…”
With his companions dropping one after another, the remaining Smoked Meat had gone pale as a sheet.
“I-it really was you, Itsuki-sama! This unworthy Mald has no right to lift his head, having failed to recognize the truth. B-but please, I beg you, at least show mercy to me alone.”
He pleaded for his life, sweating profusely all the while.
“I don’t think saving just yourself would exactly work in your favor…”
Even Father looked utterly exasperated, down to his very core.

“How very transparent… Even if I generously forgive the fact that I didn’t recognize you at first, ambushing and knocking out demi-humans and beastfolk who spoke to you in good faith, then selling them off to slave traders—I hardly think that counts as something a self-proclaimed champion of justice ought to be doing. After everything I explicitly told you was forbidden, I wonder just what these ears of yours were listening to.”
Itsuki gave the Smoked Meat’s ear a hard, deliberate yank with all his strength.
